title: Formalisme algébrique des correspondances et algèbres de Poincaré-Hodge (cf conjectures standard) : notes manuscrites (s.d.), tapuscrit annoté (s.d.), lettres (1966-1967).

deep.reconstruction:
This is the closing page of a letter, apparently to John Coates, accompanying Grothendieck's talk on the standard conjectures. The next page begins a follow-up letter 'Dear Coates' dated 6.1.1966. The page continues the list of 'known facts' started on the previous page.

(0) Historical remark. Let X be a smooth projective surface. The Künneth projectors π_i ∈ H^{4-i}(X)⊗H^i(X) ⊂ H^4(X×X) are algebraic, i.e. classes of algebraic correspondences.
- π_0 and π_4 are trivial: [pt×X] and [X×pt].
- π_1 and π_3 come from the Picard and Albanese varieties.
- π_2 = Δ − π_0 − π_1 − π_3 − π_4.
So the Künneth conjecture C(X) holds for surfaces. Tate told Grothendieck this was already noted by Hodge, 'Algebraic correspondences between surfaces', Proc. LMS (2) 44 (1938), p.226. Grothendieck remarks that it had been forgotten for nearly thirty years.

(2) Characteristic 0. Here A(X) is the Lefschetz-type conjecture: L^{n-2i} induces a bijection A^i(X) → A^{n-i}(X) on algebraic classes. It holds for dim X ≤ 4. For i ≤ 1 one uses hard Lefschetz, which identifies Hodge classes in H^{2n-2} (and H^{2n-4} when n = 4) with L-images of Hodge classes in H^2, together with the Lefschetz (1,1) theorem. The first open case is dim X = 5, in the critical degree: L: A^2 → A^3. Proving surjectivity would need the Hodge conjecture for codimension-2 classes.

Grothendieck points to the most interesting 5-dimensional case: X×Y with X a threefold and Y a hyperplane section (a surface). Via the proposition on the previous page (criteria (iv), (iv bis), (v), (vi)), A(X×Y)^0 would give C(X), i.e. algebraicity of Λ on the threefold. A naive approach goes through A(X×X), of dimension 6; this uses a 5-dimensional product instead. Hence 'the main problems arise already for 1-cycles on threefolds', even in characteristic 0.

Promise. Prompted by Kleiman, he says he will revisit old notes in which he 'pretends' to reduce the 'strong' form of Lefschetz to the 'weak' one.

Retracted strategy. He had suggested by phone a scheme: every X is birational to a smooth X' which is a specialization of a smooth X'' birational to a smooth hypersurface. Serre objected that this fails, and the objection is valid:
- π_1 is a birational invariant of smooth projective varieties.
- For smooth proper families, the specialization map π_1(generic geometric fibre) → π_1(special fibre) is surjective (SGA1).
- Smooth hypersurfaces of dimension ≥ 2 are simply connected.
So X would be simply connected. Any reduction to hypersurfaces therefore has to admit singular hypersurfaces, and needs a formulation of the standard conjectures for singular varieties.
errors: The bibliographic details of the Hodge reference (title and page) come from Tate and are only partly verifiable here. The title is given as 'Algebraic correspondances between surfaces' and 'Seeies' is a typo for 'Series'.
Serre's objection implicitly assumes dim ≥ 2. Plane curves are not simply connected, but the reduction would only matter in higher dimension, so this is harmless.

ideas.what: Künneth components of a smooth projective surface are algebraic (C(X) for dim ≤ 2); attribution to Hodge 1938
ideas.modern_name: Künneth standard conjecture for surfaces; Chow–Künneth decomposition (Murre 1990) is the motivic refinement
ideas.usually_credited_to: Grothendieck/Kleiman (standard conjectures, 1968); Murre for Chow–Künneth of surfaces
ideas.where_published: Grothendieck, 'Standard conjectures on algebraic cycles' (Bombay 1968) lists dim ≤ 2 as known; the Hodge attribution is unsure

ideas.what: Lefschetz-type conjecture A(X) known in char 0 for dim ≤ 4; first open case is the critical degree in dim 5
ideas.modern_name: Lefschetz standard conjecture, weak form A(X), via hard Lefschetz + Lefschetz (1,1)
ideas.where_published: Kleiman, 'Algebraic cycles and the Weil conjectures' (Dix exposés) discusses similar facts

ideas.what: Reduction of B/C(X) for a threefold X to A(X×Y)^0 for a 5-fold, with Y a hyperplane section, instead of A(X×X) of dim 6
ideas.modern_name: Lefschetz standard conjecture for 1-cycles on threefolds; the hyperplane-section criterion for B(X)
ideas.usually_credited_to: Kleiman (criteria for B(X) via hyperplane sections, 1968/1994)
ideas.where_published: Similar criteria appear in Kleiman's 1968 exposé; the specific 5-fold reduction is not recalled in print

ideas.what: Impossibility of reducing to smooth hypersurfaces through birational equivalence plus specialization, because of π_1 (Serre's objection)
ideas.modern_name: Specialization of π_1 (SGA1 X) and birational invariance of π_1

ideas.what: Need to formulate standard conjectures for singular varieties in order to reduce to hypersurfaces
ideas.modern_name: Standard conjectures for singular varieties / intersection cohomology versions
ideas.usually_credited_to: Later work after the decomposition theorem, e.g. de Cataldo–Migliorini; Corti–Hanamura on motivic intersection cohomology

missed.claim: Grothendieck had 'old scribbles' purporting to reduce the strong form of the Lefschetz standard conjecture (B) to the weak one (A). These notes are not known in print.
missed.quote: I will look again at my old scribbles on that subject (when I pretend to reduce the "strong" form of Lefschetz to the "week" one)
missed.why_it_might_matter_today: Whether B(X) follows from A applied to auxiliary varieties is still central. B is open even for threefolds in char 0. Any such reduction in the archive (cf. the proposition on the preceding pages) would be of interest.

missed.claim: Program: reduce the standard conjectures to hypersurfaces. This requires formulating them for singular varieties, since Serre's π_1 obstruction rules out smooth models.
missed.quote: one will have to work also with singular ones, and see how to reformulate for singular varieties the standard conjectures
missed.why_it_might_matter_today: This anticipates intersection-cohomology formulations of Lefschetz/Hodge-type standard conjectures. The hypersurface-reduction strategy itself, and its obstruction, is not a standard part of the literature.

missed.claim: Historical record: Grothendieck, via Tate, credits Hodge (1938) with the algebraicity of the Künneth components for surfaces, which he says had fallen into oblivion.
missed.quote: pointed out (Tate tells me) by Hodge in Algebraic correspondances between surfaces ... has fallen into oblivion for nearly thirty years
missed.why_it_might_matter_today: A minor attribution point for the history of Künneth/Chow–Künneth decompositions of surfaces.

deep.surprise_reason: Mostly known facts and a retracted idea. Mildly notable: the explicit reduction of the threefold case to A(X×Y)^0 for a 5-fold; the mention of unpublished 'scribbles' reducing strong Lefschetz to weak Lefschetz; and the hypersurface-reduction strategy with Serre's π_1 obstruction and the call for singular versions.
transcription_corrections: 'Seeies' is Grothendieck's typo for 'Series'; 'Soc.' has an overstruck character in the image.
Handwritten insertion 'nearly' above 'thirty years' (the transcription has it correctly).
Typed text shows 'Kleimanx' with an overtyped character; it means Kleiman.
'week' (sic, for 'weak'), 'spcialisation', 'birati[o]nally' (overtyped) and 'somehaw' (overtyped, = somehow) are typos in the original typescript.
'A(X)^0': the superscript is a small circle, the same 'critical dimension' symbol written ^∘ on the previous page.
